summary: Describes architectures for recording sessions in a Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) environment. Recording is needed in places like call centers and financial trading, often for regulatory reasons, and is usually done by sending a copy of the media stream to a recording device.

eli5.summary: Some phone calls must be saved, like in a bank. This describes the ways to quietly make a copy of the call and send it to a recorder.

questions: what is a session recording client
can a sip proxy record calls
subtitle: How a SIP environment copies a call's media and metadata to a recording server, and where the copying can happen.

tldr.problem: Call centers and financial trading often must record every call for regulatory, compliance and consumer protection reasons, and SIP had no common architecture for it.
tldr.mechanism: A Session Recording Client (SRC) opens a separate SIP Recording Session with a Session Recording Server (SRS) and sends it a copy of the media (Replicated Media) plus Recording Metadata; either side may start that session.
tldr.outcome: The RFC gives the architecture and leaves the actual SIP extensions and metadata formats to companion documents. It covers only active recording of users who know they are recorded.

facts.label: Can a SIP proxy be an SRC

today: RFC 7245 is an Informational document with no listed obsoleting or updating RFC. The SIP extensions and metadata formats it relies on are defined in companion documents that it names as work in progress.

sections.title: Purpose and Scope
sections.content:
Recording a session is typically done by sending a copy of a media stream to a recording device. This RFC describes architectures for doing that in a SIP environment, building on the use cases and requirements in RFC 6341. It focuses on how sessions are set up between the SRC and the SRS to carry the Replicated Media and Recording Metadata (for example, who is involved).

Several things are out of scope: archiving and retrieval, passive recording (a device detecting media from the network, for example by port mirroring), and lawful intercept. The Recording Session uses normal INVITE-initiated dialogs per RFC 3261 and SDP per RFC 4566, with some SIP extensions expected. Replicated Media is sent in real time and is not buffered by the SRC.
sections.eli5: This paper is about making a copy of a call on purpose and sending it to a recorder. It is not about secretly listening in.

sections.title: The Roles
sections.content:
The Communication Session (CS) is the call being recorded. The Recording Session (RS) is the separate SIP session between an SRC and an SRS made to record it. The SRC is a logical function that acts as the source of recorded media and metadata; in practice it could be a SIP phone, a media gateway, a Session Border Controller or a media server with an application server. The SRS is a SIP user agent acting as the sink, typically a multi-port device receiving from many sources at once.

The RFC also defines recording-aware user agents, which understand SIP extensions that signal recording or express preferences to start, pause, resume or stop it, and recording-unaware ones, which must be handled by other means outside the architecture.
sections.eli5: There is the call, a copier who makes a copy, and a recorder who receives it. Some callers understand the recording signals and some do not.

sections.title: Where the Recording Client Can Live
sections.content:
The SRC is a logical function that can sit in, or be split across, several components:

  • B2BUA: a back-to-back user agent with access to the media can be the SRC. It is responsible for notifying the users that the call is recorded and for honoring requests or policies that say not to record.
  • Endpoint: a SIP endpoint can be the SRC and send the Replicated Media itself.
  • SIP proxy: it cannot be an SRC, because it has no access to the media.
  • MEDIACTRL: either the SRC or SRS can be built from an application server controlling a media server, following RFC 5567.
  • Conference focus: a focus and mixer can act as the SRC, sending mixed media or one stream per participant, and a participant can also be the SRC.
sections.eli5: The copier can be a helper in the middle of the call, one of the phones itself, or a conference host. A mere message passer cannot be one because it never hears the voices.

sections.title: Setting Up and Controlling the Recording Session
sections.content:
Either side may start the RS, and the RS is independent of the CS at both the SIP dialog and session levels. An SRC that starts it is provisioned with the SRS URI, resolved by RFC 3263 procedures, sends an INVITE marked as being for recording, and uses a=sendonly on each media line to start now or a=inactive if not ready. An SRS that starts it sends an INVITE to the SRC, identifies the sessions to record, and uses a=recvonly or a=inactive. If the SRS does not know what media is available, it can use an offerless INVITE so the SRC makes the first SDP offer.

Either side can pause recording by changing the direction to inactive and resume by changing it back to recvonly or sendonly. For a two-way audio call, the two streams may be mixed into one at the SRC or sent as two separate streams. The CS and RS are negotiated separately, which may force the SRC to transcode. Lossless recording, where regulation demands it, may need network QoS, reliable transport and protocol capabilities together.

Metadata follows the model in a companion document and is carried by SIP-based mechanisms defined there; non-SIP delivery is out of scope. Users are typically told by an announcement or tones, and SIPREC adds an indication in the SIP messages. The SRC notifies all UAs whose media it replicates.
sections.eli5: Either the copier or the recorder can ring the other to start. They can press pause by saying they are not sending or receiving for now, and press play again later.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RS is a standard SIP dialog and media session, so it uses existing SIP security mechanisms. The architecture is intended only where users know they are recorded; it is not for lawful intercept, which requires that users are not told.

The SRS must protect stored content with a cipher at least as strong as the original, and keep keys secure and release them only to authorized parties. Protection of the RS should not be weaker than the CS and may need to be stronger, since the media is retransmitted. The SRC must authenticate the SRS; implementations must be able to do mutual authentication. If media is decrypted on the CS and re-encrypted on the RS, a new key must be used. Retrieval is out of scope, but retrievers should be authenticated carefully.
sections.eli5: The copy of the call must be locked at least as tightly as the original, and the copier must check it is really talking to the right recorder.

left.title: SRC-initiated
left.desc: INVITE with a=sendonly (or a=inactive if not ready).

right.title: SRS-initiated
right.desc: INVITE with a=recvonly (or a=inactive if not ready).
